wrong options / checks: also accepted: london is smaller than riga
explanation shown to learner: Both city orders form a correct sentence: subject + *is smaller than* + the other city. This task checks grammar, not geography.
explanation in Latvian: Abas pilsētu secības veido pareizu teikumu: teikuma priekšmets + *is smaller than* + otra pilsēta. Uzdevums pārbauda gramatiku, nevis ģeogrāfiju.

task: Match each sentence with what we know about the action.
correct answer: I've been reading, but I haven't finished the book. = The reading is not finished. ; I've read the whole book. = The reading is finished. ; I've been waiting since nine and I'm still here. = The waiting continues now. ; I've written all five emails and sent them. = The emails are ready and sent.
explanation shown to learner: Read the whole sentence: *not finished* and *still here* show continuing actions; *the whole book* and *all five emails ... sent* show completed results.
explanation in Latvian: Izlasi visu teikumu: *not finished* un *still here* norāda uz turpinātu darbību; *the whole book* un *all five emails ... sent* — uz pabeigtu rezultātu.
replaces: I've been reading. = the activity ; I've read three chapters. = the result ; I've been waiting for an hour. = how long ; I've written five emails. = how many

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: Put the words in order to make a question.
correct answer: will you be at home when the parcel arrives
wrong options / checks: also accepted: when the parcel arrives will you be at home
explanation shown to learner: In the question, put *will* before *you*. After *when*, use *arrives* for the future, not *will arrive*.
explanation in Latvian: Jautājumā liec *will* pirms *you*. Pēc *when* nākotnes nozīmē lieto *arrives*, nevis *will arrive*.
replaces: will you be at home when the parcel arrives

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: The final is tomorrow. I don't think the team ___ the match. (win)
explanation shown to learner: An opinion about the future: *I think / don't think* + *will*.
explanation in Latvian: Viedoklis par nākotni: *I think / don't think + will.*
replaces: I don't think the team ___ the match.

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: We ___ the kitchen next month. We've already chosen the colour. (paint)
correct answer: are going to paint | are painting
explanation shown to learner: A plan or arrangement: *are going to paint* or *are painting*.
explanation in Latvian: Plāns vai vienošanās: *are going to paint* vai *are painting*.
answer notes: are painting :: Correct: *are painting* presents this as an arrangement. *Are going to paint* presents it as an existing plan. :: Pareizi: *are painting* parāda norunātu pasākumu. *Are going to paint* parāda jau pieņemtu plānu.

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: Join with when: I'll finish the report. Then I'll call you.
correct answer: I'll call you when I finish the report. | I'll call you when I've finished the report. | When I finish the report, I'll call you. | When I've finished the report, I'll call you.
explanation shown to learner: After *when* we use *finish* or *have finished* for the future, not *will finish*. The main clause keeps *will*: *I will call you*.
explanation in Latvian: Pēc *when* nākotnes nozīmē lieto *finish* vai *have finished*, nevis *will finish*. Galvenajā daļā paliek *will*: *I will call you*.

topic: Future: will, going to, present continuous
task: Choose the correct option: We ___ some friends for dinner this Saturday. We've arranged it, so I need to go shopping.
explanation shown to learner: *Are having* describes an arrangement for this Saturday. The other forms describe past situations.
explanation in Latvian: *Are having* apzīmē norunātu pasākumu šajā sestdienā. Pārējās formas apraksta pagātnes situācijas.
replaces: Choose the correct option: We ___ some friends for dinner on Saturday, so I need to go shopping.

task:
A: I've hurt my hand.
B: How ___ you ___ that? (do)
explanation shown to learner: New information: present perfect; the details after it: past simple.
explanation in Latvian: *Jaunums*: Present Perfect; sīkāk pēc tam: Past Simple.
replaces: A: I've burnt myself. B: How ___ you ___ that? (do)

topic: Narrative tenses with past perfect continuous
task: Tom was tired when he got home. He ___ hard all day. (work)
explanation shown to learner: *had been* + *-ing*: an activity that went on before a moment in the past, often with a result you can see.
explanation in Latvian: *had been + -ing*: darbība, kas *ilga* pirms kāda brīža pagātnē, bieži ar redzamu rezultātu.
replaces: Use the past perfect, the past perfect continuous or the present perfect continuous: Tom was tired when he got home. He ___ hard all day. (work)
answer notes: had worked :: Correct too: *had worked* focuses on the work completed before he got home. *Had been working* emphasises its duration and explains his tiredness. :: Arī pareizi: *had worked* uzsver pirms pārnākšanas paveikto. *Had been working* uzsver ilgumu un izskaidro nogurumu.

task: Match each word with the form that fits 'I have ___ it.'
correct answer: write = written ; take = taken ; see = seen ; break = broken
explanation shown to learner: Learn the past participle with each irregular verb: *write → written*, *take → taken*, *see → seen*, *break → broken*.
explanation in Latvian: Neregulārie darbības vārdi: iemācies 3. formu kopā ar darbības vārdu.
replaces: write = written ; take = taken ; see = seen ; go = gone
